flags.observation: Lore claim absent; power "the squash match destroys them" carries the whole line, and "them" has no referent.
"boiling point, trap" tacks on the power label plus the Power stat value; ends like a rulebook tag.
"hardcore valet, daggers" stacks a label and an image right after "dagger hits"; duplicate word, list fragment, weak landing.
"the botch, password" keeps the power's card reference as a bare keyword; mechanic survives as term, not as picture.
118 characters with opener; "thieves" three times and "gold" twice inside one beat, hard to say in one breath.
"So Aladdin's cave" fuses Ali Baba with Aladdin's cave; cards never link them, so the causal "So" rests on nothing.
"But the cave has teeth" precedes a Sinbad-voyage giant; the image belongs to The Magic Cave, seven cards later.
Openers lean on objects and places ("the brass answers", "an island moves", "the rusted decree"); Tip 3, people with wants, rarely served.
Eight openers across twenty-eight cards, under the one-third floor, spaced at near-fixed intervals; "At dawn:" echoes beat 2 verbatim.
"Dunyazad's heat" calls back to the directly preceding card; formally a callback, but no distance, no memory payoff.
Two short intro beats offer a pun but never set up the territory or storytelling-for-survival premise; satirical provocation stays thin.
Outro reuses "blade" and "sentence" from the intro; callback present, yet no turn beyond the opening setup.
